name: Gallery zoom tour
looks: One tile fills the frame, then the camera pulls back to reveal it is part of a live grid, whips sideways into a different tile until that one fills the frame, and match-cuts straight into that tile's own scene. It plays as one continuous camera move through many pieces rather than a series of cuts.
build: Lay out absolutely positioned cards (or three.js planes) in one large world container, and drive a pseudo-camera as focus x, focus y and a log scale so the zoom speed feels even; tween each tile's corner radius to zero as it reaches full-bleed, and play each tile's own content from the clock even while small.
sound: A soft shift on the pull-back and a whoosh on each whip.
prompt: Start zoomed into one tile, pull the camera back to reveal a grid of many live tiles, whip into a different one until it fills the frame, then cut straight into that tile's own scene. Use this single continuous camera move to show a portfolio, a set of features, or several examples side by side, keeping to one camera move at a time.
source: prompt-motion.com's own promo, in its gallery of Claude-made motion films, studied 2026-10-07.
